To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
for data intensive monitoring application, in-sensor processing results in lower energy consumption than raw data transmission, irrespective of the radio technology used.
in-sensor data processing is more energy efficient than raw data transmission for high sample rate monitoring application.

in-sensor computation is a more energy efficient solution for data intensive monitoring application as compared to raw data transmission, and the energy consumption for raw data transmission using Wi-Fi is the least among the three technologies considered in this paper.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy efficient design of a wireless sensor node that performs data intensive monitoring.

the energy consumption analysis of two data intensive applications, namely temperature monitoring and ECG monitoring, using different short range technologies, namely ZigBee, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and Wi-Fi.
the design and implementation of a novel wireless sensing platform, and its application in two high-data rate applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy consumption of in-sensor computation is lower than raw data transmission, but the gap between them decreases with increasing data rate.
in-sensor data processing is more energy efficient for high data rate monitoring applications.
in-sensor data processing is a better choice than raw data transmission for energy constrained wireless sensing nodes, even when the wireless link is error-free.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in-sensor computation is an effective approach for energy efficient data intensive wireless sensing applications.
in-sensor computation should be preferred for data intensive monitoring application in the presence of energy constraints.
in-sensor data processing is a viable option to realize high sample-rate monitoring applications using low-power wireless sensor networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in-sensor processing should be considered as a viable alternative for energy constrained data intensive monitoring applications.
in-sensor computation should be considered as a viable alternative to raw data transmission, particularly for applications with high sampling rates.
in-sensor data processing should be considered in order to minimize energy consumption in wireless sensing systems.
